public_rationale: The claim has an ordinary testable reading, but the reviewed financing surveys do not measure the arrangement Marcus describes. The original news report concerns one proposed deal and cannot establish what comparable startups typically accept. Treating liquidation preferences as equivalent to ongoing-profit sharing would overstate the evidence.
limitations: The comparison group and historical window require interpretation.
Semafor is used as reporting about negotiations because no executed agreement was obtained.
The condition concerning the accuracy of the rumored terms remains unverified in this record.

statement.excerpt: That’s a lot, and not the sort of thing that a rocketship startup would typically agree to.
statement.document_title: Is Microsoft about to get the deal of the century? Or is Sam Altman unloading OpenAI at just the right time?

from_speaker: 75% of OpenAI’s profits until it recoups its investment
not the sort of thing that a rocketship startup would typically agree to
our_interpretation: Rocketship startup means a rapidly growing startup with strong financing prospects.
The test concerns whether this profit-allocation arrangement was customary, rather than whether any successful startup ever accepted one.
For prevailing financing practice, use the latest completed quarter with published market evidence before the post: the third quarter of 2022. The speaker supplied no comparison period.
The monetary scope records the rumored allocation percentage, not a realized profit amount. Its accounting basis is a press estimate, and the contractual definition of profits is unspecified.
The condition qualifies the application to OpenAI. The comparison of financing terms can be investigated separately from confirmation that OpenAI signed them.
criteria.support_condition: Representative financing records or a well-supported market survey show that allocating 75% of ongoing profits to one investor until repayment was unusual among comparable rapidly growing startups.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative records show that this arrangement, or a materially equivalent ongoing-profit allocation, was customary among comparable rapidly growing startups.
